preamble: The shift from the voiced labio-velar approximant [w] to the voiced labiodental fricative [v] is a widespread fortition process in the history of Indo-European languages. It involves the loss of the velar component and the strengthening of the labial constriction from an approximant to a fricative. In the Jê family, Apinajé (Northern Jê) and Laklãnõ (Southern Jê) independently changed *w to v.

examples.note: Original [w] fortified to [v] by the Middle High German period.
Classical Latin [w] became a bilabial fricative [β] and eventually a labiodental fricative [v] in most Romance varieties.

examples.to: Tongan, Niuean, Rapa Nui vaka; Samoan, Tahitian vaʻa
examples.note: *w surfaces as labiodental [v] in most Polynesian languages; Hawaiian waʻa and Māori waka keep [w]
Apinajé replaced the glides *w and *j with fricatives in stressed syllables. Mẽbêngôkre has kwêñ.
